weekend_note: Dry and sunny all weekend: highs around 71 to 72, lows in the low 50s, rain chance under 5% each day. Saturday morning is windy, with gusts that could top 40 mph on the beaches and bridges, easing by Sunday. Picks: UWF football (1 PM Saturday, tickets online only), Ice Flyers opening night (indoors at the Bay Center), fall baseball at Blue Wahoos Stadium, comedian Ali Siddiq at the Saenger (indoors) and Barktoberfest downtown on Sunday. Escambia schools reopen Monday.

news.title: Two Isaias resource centers open in Pensacola through Oct 30
news.summary: Residents can get recovery help at the Bayview Senior Center and the Salvation Army building on N Q Street, 7 AM to 7 PM daily through Oct 30. They connect people with aid but do not hand out food or supplies; free bus rides are offered.

news.title: DeSantis asks for broader federal disaster declaration
news.summary: Only a presidential emergency declaration covering public facilities is in place so far. A page note says the governor submitted the wider FEMA request Thursday night. Escambia's public damage is estimated at $64 million, and residents are urged to report damage.

news.title: FPL regional leader gives update on remaining outages
news.summary: FPL Northwest Florida's J.T. Young appeared on WEAR Thursday to discuss restoration. The details are in the video, so no outage numbers are reported here.

news.title: USPS says postal operations are back across North Florida
news.summary: The Postal Service's Florida 1 District said all facilities resumed operations Thursday after the storm shutdown.

news.title: Community Health Northwest Florida reopens most clinics
news.summary: All but three sites are open again, and the Palafox Street clinic resumes full services. Pediatrics on 12th Avenue and the Pine Forest High and C.A. Weis school clinics stay closed without power.

news.title: Suspect arrested after Nine Mile Road bank robbery
news.summary: Deputies say a 32-year-old man was caught after a Thursday holdup at a bank on W Nine Mile Road. He is held without bond.

news.title: Escambia County debris pickup under way, expected to take months
news.summary: Officials expect three to four months of cleanup with several rounds and warn against paying unlicensed yard workers. Carried over from the Oct 16 update.

coverage_note: Written overnight Saturday Oct 17. The forecast is AccuWeather's Pensacola daily forecast (8 days); other sites put lows a few degrees higher (low-to-mid 50s) and all show under 5% rain. NorthEscambia.com could not be fetched, so north county events come from the Allevents Cantonment listing (Cantonment, Gonzalez, Barrineau Park) and are listed as posted, with details left as 'See event page'. Sparse Gonzalez coverage. News is from WEAR articles dated Oct 14 to 16; Local Pulse and the City of Pensacola pages could not be opened tonight. No restaurant openings or closings were confirmed; Pelican Bar and Grill, Casa Luvia and Launch remain unconfirmed. Saenger, Ice Flyers (opponent for Oct 17 conflicts between sources) and Blue Wahoos first-pitch times were not confirmed. Most carried-over events were not rechecked.
